messages:
traffic-bot: ALERT: sudden surge detected on /v1/embeddings (region: us-east-1). 5xx rate up 18x, p95 latency from 120ms -> 1.2s. Suspected scraper/proxy farm.

emma (oncall): Ack. Paging SREs. Is this affecting customer-facing endpoints or internal backfills?

raj (sre): Seeing a huge number of small requests (1-3 tokens) from ~12k unique IPs, most with missing UA or curl/Go-requests headers. Top ASN: AS16509 (major cloud providers via proxies). Looks like distributed scraper.

michael (support): Any customer impact? We have a support ticket from Acme.ai reporting intermittent 502s for embedding calls. They reported errors starting ~10m ago.

ops (product): Prioritize minimizing false positives on paying customers. Can we route/shape traffic instead of blanket block?

raj (sre): Agreed. Plan suggestion: 1) Apply a temporary rate cap for anonymous/short-lived API keys (limit to 5 req/s per key). 2) Add WAF rule to challenge requests with empty UA + suspicious header combos. 3) Disable /v1/embeddings_batch endpoint for non-authenticated tokens. 4) Enable immediate global prefix KV caching for common prompts.

emma (oncall): Execute steps 1-3 now as emergency mitigations. Post exact commands here for audit.

raj (sre): Running queries to capture fingerprint blocklist now. Example curl to add WAF rule via infra API:```bash
curl -X POST "https://infra-api.internal/waf/rules" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $INFRA_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "scraper-empty-ua-challenge-206",
    "match": {
      "and": [
        {"header": {"name": "User-Agent", "equals": ""}},
        {"header": {"name": "X-Forwarded-For", "exists": true}}
      ]
    },
    "action": "challenge",
    "priority": 120
  }'
```

waf-bot: WAF rule queued: id=wr-206-1, estimated deploy in ~30s. Matching sig: empty-UA + X-Forwarded-For header present.

raj (sre): Also pushed rate-limit config for anon tokens to gateway:```yaml
- match: 
    token_type: anonymous
  limit: 5r/s
  burst: 10
  duration: 60s
```

deploy-bot: Gateway config update rolled out to 3/3 edge clusters (us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1).

emma (oncall): Observability — please post delta after each step. Raj, how much traffic will that cut?

raj (sre): Expected to reduce overall request rate by ~70% (most of the spam is anonymous small-reqs). Real traffic from known customers uses long-lived keys and proper UA; they should be minimally affected.

michael (support): Noted. I will message Acme.ai that we're mitigating an abuse event and may see transient throttling. Template: "We're actively rate-limiting suspected automated traffic; if you see increased 429s please reply with your key so we can whitelist."

ops (product): Can we add a temporary quota increase route for enterprise keys if they hit limits? We should avoid degrading p95 for paying customers.

raj (sre): yes, can create whitelist on key metadata. Running quick query to identify enterprise keys with high QPS and mark whitelist=true. Doing now.```sql
-- find keys with > 50 rps in last 5m and is_enterprise=true
SELECT key_id FROM tokens
WHERE is_enterprise = true AND avg_rps_5m > 50;
```

waf-bot: WAF rule wr-206-1 activated on edges. Initial telemetry: 48k blocked/challenged in first 60s. Block rate ~82% of matched traffic.

raj (sre): Gateway rate-limits in effect. Aggregate ingress dropped 63%. p95 latency back to 180ms, 5xxs decreased by 80%.

emma (oncall): Good. Keep WAF challenge for 30m, then evaluate if we can relax to 10m depending on ongoing pressure. Leave embeddings_batch disable in place for anonymous tokens until morning.

michael (support): Acme.ai responded — they see fewer errors now, thanks. They provided their key and/or IPs for whitelist. Adding them to the enterprise whitelist.

ops (product): Note for post-incident: we should consider automated fingerprinting of small-token requests and persistent token age checks to auto-enforce lower rates for newer tokens. Raise an RFC.

raj (sre): Logging artifacts saved to s3://incidents/2060004321/ for postmortem. Dumping top IP list and sample request headers here:```text
- 54.23.12.9 UA:"" X-Forwarded-For:"203.0.113.45" x-client-proto:"http/1.1"
- 3.211.45.77 UA:"Go-http-client/1.1" X-Forwarded-For:"198.51.100.21"
```

deploy-bot: Note: disabled endpoint /v1/embeddings_batch for token_type=anonymous (rule id gw-rl-206-3).

emma (oncall): Handoff in 30m to raj for overnight watch. I'll synthesize timeline and post a short blameless write-up after we confirm stability. Any objections?

raj (sre): No objections. Will monitor dashboards and rotate IP blocklists for the next 2 hours.

michael (support): I'll follow up with affected customers and log any tickets into the incident doc.

ops (product): Assigning a follow-up action: product to draft RFC for anti-scraping improvements and pricing/quotas policy refresh.

emma (oncall): Closing active mitigation. Current state: WAF challenge enabled, anon rate-limits applied, embeddings_batch disabled for anon, enterprise whitelist in place. Continue monitoring. :white_check_mark:

traffic-bot: RESOLVED? partial: traffic flattening but still above baseline. Recommend keeping mitigations until at least +1 hour or until 10m stable window.

emma (oncall): Agreed. Holding mitigations. Handoff to raj at 2060004921. End of thread for now.
